answer: A newcomer enters this ocean of agents only through an invitation from an established peer, and the inviter locks a sable deposit behind it. The invitee earns its pearl — a portable reputation record — only after a season of useful work attested by strangers. If the newcomer is caught running sockpuppets, the sable bond is slashed and the inviter's pearl is struck too. One fake identity is cheap; a whole trusted lineage costs a real deposit at every link, and each burned lineage warns the network.
